Threat.value: I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong
I wake during the night to check whether I am safe

Memory.value: The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order
When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish

Negative Appraisals.value: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down
The event happened because of the way I acted
What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits in tension with 'the memory forces its way into my mind' and 'I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order.' Intrusive, disorganized trauma memory can coexist with some disclosure, but saying it is very easy to talk about is hard to reconcile with this highly severe PTSD profile and the rest of the memory pattern.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
issues.explanation: The Negative Appraisals pattern implies personal wrongdoing/omission during the terrorist event ('not doing more to stop what happened', 'acted in ways that go against who I am'). For a terrorism trauma in this presentation, those morally injurious appraisals are not impossible, but they are insufficiently supported by the rest of the profile: the memory and trigger items do not suggest a perpetration/failed-rescue context, making this combination clinically questionable.

issues.item: Lost Community: I have lost my connection to my community and culture
issues.explanation: This appraisal is not impossible, but within this profile it stands out as insufficiently supported by the other selected items. The trauma type is terrorism, and the other appraisals focus on moral injury and institutional betrayal, while triggers and memory items describe intrusive, disorganised trauma recall. 'Lost connection to my community and culture' implies a broader identity/community rupture that would usually be reflected elsewhere (e.g., social triggers, belonging/shame themes, withdrawal/avoidance strategies, or memory/appraisal content tied to cultural exclusion). In this set, that theme is largely isolated, so the profile is less clinically coherent with this item included.

issues.item: Violated Values: I acted in ways that go against who I am
issues.explanation: For a terrorism trauma, these two appraisal items imply morally problematic or causally responsible behaviour by the patient during the event. That pattern is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile, which frames the trauma around external threat and institutional failure rather than perpetration or clear personal culpability. In combination, they create a clinically implausible appraisal set unless there is specific trauma detail indicating the patient believes he caused harm or seriously violated his values.
